CONFIDENCE: 0.6
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows signatures of a methyl-substituted primary amine:  
• Two sharp X–H bands at 3385 cm⁻¹ and 3328 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of the asymmetric and symmetric N–H stretches of an –NH₂ group (rule GFQ-002).  
• Three C–H stretching bands at 2967, 2905 and 2828 cm⁻¹ match the typical CH₃ asymmetric, symmetric and “Fermi-type” stretches of a methyl group attached to a heteroatom (rule GFQ-003).  
• A strong band at 1037 cm⁻¹ fits the C–N stretching region for aliphatic amines (rule GFQ-010).  
• The 1479 cm⁻¹ band corresponds to the CH₃ bending deformation normally found near 1450 cm⁻¹ (rule GFQ-003).  

Among the candidates, only methylamine (SMILES “CN”, candidate 1) contains both a CH₃ group and a primary amine capable of giving two N–H stretches. Other candidates either lack NH₂ (e.g., ethanol “CO”, nitromethane 3, diazo compounds 4–5, 7) or possess additional heteroatoms/bonds that should generate diagnostic peaks not observed. Therefore the spectrum is most consistent with methylamine.
